How to choose an uptime monitoring plan

Put your monitor count, check interval and status-page need into the calculator to price UptimeRobot, Better Stack, Hyperping, Pingdom and self-hosted Uptime Kuma side by side. These are the questions to settle before you trust the answer.

Why does the cheapest uptime monitor change as I add monitors?

Plans are tiers, not per-unit prices. UptimeRobot's free plan covers 50 monitors at five-minute checks, but 60-second checks need a paid tier, and past 100 monitors you jump to the next one. Better Stack adds a per-monitor fee after its included monitors, while Pingdom steps through fixed 10, 50, 100 and 500-check plans. The cheapest provider at 10 monitors is rarely the cheapest at 120, which is what the crossover table shows.

Which check interval do I actually need?

Match it to how long an outage may go unnoticed. A five-minute check can miss a four-minute outage entirely and delays the alert by up to five minutes; 60 seconds is the usual paid default and 30 seconds or faster costs the most. If your SLA promises 99.9 percent monthly (about 43 minutes of downtime), a 3 or 5 minute interval is usually fine; for payment or login flows pay for 60 seconds or less.

Should I self-host Uptime Kuma?

It is free software and a small VPS runs hundreds of monitors, so it is cheapest on paper. The catches: the monitor must not live on the infrastructure it watches, you maintain and patch it, and you need a second independent way to alert you when the monitor itself dies. Many teams self-host for volume and keep one hosted monitor watching the self-hosted one.

No warranty. This page is provided free and as-is, without warranty of any kind. It is not financial or engineering advice; verify prices at each vendor. Best-effort hosting, no SLA.

What will uptime monitoring cost for your monitors and check interval, and who is cheapest?

Enter the number of monitors, how often they must be checked and whether you need a public status page. Get UptimeRobot, Better Stack, Hyperping, Pingdom and self-hosted Uptime Kuma priced side by side, the 12-month spend as you add monitors, and the monitor count where the cheapest option changes — before a tier jump surprises you.

Prefer a CLI, or want a budget gate in CI?

node cli.mjs compare --monitors 60 --interval-sec 60 --status-page --growth 5
node cli.mjs compare --monitors 60 --interval-sec 60 --provider pingdom --budget 50   # exit 1 over budget

Get cli.mjs and engine.mjs — Node 18+, nothing to install, no network call. More: how to choose an uptime-monitoring plan.

Common questions

Does this check my sites?

No. It uses only the monitor count, interval and status-page need you type, and plan tables you can edit. It never contacts your sites or the vendors. Treat every figure as a way to compare options, never as what you will be charged.

Where do the prices come from?

They are approximate public list prices as best known in 2025 on monthly billing, shown with an as-of line, and every plan is editable. Vendors change plans often, so check each pricing page before deciding.

What is not included?

SMS and phone-call alert credits, extra seats, multi-location or transaction (browser) checks, annual-billing discounts, taxes, and each vendor's fair-use terms. Alerting and seats often cost more than the monitors themselves, so use this to compare the monitor lines, not to forecast the whole invoice.

Is my data uploaded anywhere?

No. The page calculates in your browser and sends nothing. The CLI reads local files and makes no network call.
